Messages.Author: Steve Wieck
Messages.Body:
Hello All,

Just a note on the timing of the expansions to come after Anarchs. The
player base, as represented by those of you who post on the newsgroup and
forum, has been pretty clear on a preference of V:TES expansions coming
about every 9 months or even a year. We listened to you and adopted that
time frame between expansions (Anarchs coming almost 10 months after Cam Ed
which came about 10 months after Bloodlines).

We are however changing to a six month interval between expansions for both
Black Hand which will come in November and then for the expansion to follow
Black Hand coming in 2004. We have a couple important reasons for doing
this, including:
1. Hobby game retailers are overwhelmed by the number of game products that
are released every week of every year. When a game only comes onto their
"radar screen" once every year, then that game never achieves any sort of
prominence in their store. Retailers are more accustomed to two or three or
more releases per year from any active card game. Both retailer feedback and
specific sales data show us how V:TES drops out of retailer's vision when it
has been too many months since the last release forced them to take note of
the game and stock both new and prior expansions.
2. The expansion following Black Hand will relate to other White Wolf
products released in early 2004, so we cannot hold it back more than 6
months after Black Hand.

Knowing that this pace is faster than many of you prefer, we will aim to
keep the size of these next two expansions modest - to a size similar to
Anarchs. We understand that everyone has time and/or money constraints and
we don't intend to expand the game faster than casual play and purchase can
allow a player to remain current with the game's expansion. After these next
two expansions we expect to resume a nine month interval between expansions.

Steve Wieck
White Wolf

"vermillian" <vermillian....@web2news.net> wrote in message news:3246...@web2news.com...

> 1.) White wolf makes more money doing this. WW with money means VTES
> stays alive.

I guess the happy compromise is a greater percentage of
new cards in a starter. Perhaps changing the starter to these X cards and
the rest random?

But if profit was the main motivation why didn't we see 6 new starters in
Anarchs? It can't be because of the number of new cards that would be needed
because thats only 4 cards per starter!

The starter appears to be there to get cards reprinted, and if thats the case
why not make starters of just reprints and cards that can be acquired in boosters?
New players could buy them for the cards, and older players could spend their
money on boosters which generate more revenue per card (booster price/11
compared to starter price/100).

They could even put reprinted essential cards in boosters so long as they were
commons (which the essential cards should be anyways). 30 reprinted cards
of a 200 card set (or about half the commons being reprints)

Bloodlines had 198 new cards. Anarchs had something like 130.
So instead of me buying 2 boxes of boosters and three starters
to get my complete set I would probably buy 3, maybe 4 boxes of
boosters. WW would be making more money, not less. My situation
is not universal of course but discussions with other locals tells me I'm
not alone in this line of thinking.

> 2.) Prerelease events are better. No more of that bloodlines crappy
> prerelease (that I didn't even attend).

So without going to the bloodline pre-release you know it was not as
good as the Anarch or CE pre-releases (and knew in advance apparently)?
Regardless, bloodlines was an expansion designed to complement existing
decks. There have been numerous posts to the effect that bloodline clans were not meant to be played on their own (with ease). So
comparing recent pre-releases to
bloodlines might be a pointless exercise at best.

I think with the current booster composition, a six or eight booster pre-release for
anarchs would have done just fine. The starters were all over the map anyways
it seemed. A tournament without blood dolls, wakes, and bum's rushes? Cool!
Adds new dynamics to a deck.

But YMMV

> 3.) Gives new players better ideas of what to do with these new cards.

Not worth mentioning. I've discovered (after a weekends worth of demos)
that the new player generally learns combos best from a player explaining
a combo or having a combo used on them. They then get the feel of how
to put together a combo. At that point a booster is just as likely a source
as a deck for a source of a combo.

> 4.) Precon leagues get more exciting.

As I've never been in a precon league my experience is limited. But there
are now 17 readily available starters (with the re-release of FN & SW
starters). Having an every second expansion without starters won't kill
such a league.

Regards,
-JTP

That was kinda my point (convoluted and perhaps not well presented).
I was attempting to argue that profit isn't WW's (only) motive for starters with
starter-only cards or we would have seen more starters in anarchs.('cause I'm
sure WW enjoys profits) It would be simple for them to create new starters (ie
its not like staggering development costs are holding them back)
1.select more cards to be reprinted from CE, FN
2.create 2 new vamps per deck
3.add about 20 anarch cards from the booster sheets
and now everybody must buy 3 additional starters to complete their
set, disregarding trading.

New players don't care if their starter has cards that only appear in
starter decks, or has cards they can also get in boosters.

So doesn't it make sense for whitewolf to create starters
with no new starter-only cards for newbies?
1. experienced players would not buy many other than for sealed
deck - this would meant stock more likely to be on hand for new
players
2. Collectors would likely replace $ spent on starters with $ spent
on boosters. Which as we both pointed out should have higher
profit margins.

I've kinda gone in big circle here.... but I'm sure my point is somewhere
in the centre. Let me try to sum up:
1. Whitewolf makes more money off of boosters than starters ($/card and
less peripherals (rule books, double packaging))
2. Starters are neccessary for attracting new players
3. Whitewolf should prefer current players to buy boosters more than
starters from a profit perspective.

so:
A. Will we see a booster only set (since starters from different sets are
all currently available I argue we could go a set or two without more starters)
B. If we must have more starters why not make them with no "starter-only"
new cards.

Hopefully the answer to (A) is yes. I'm then a happy camper. If not then
I suspect the answer to (B) will be that to justify the cost of packaging and
selling any starter decks, new player sales are insufficient, therefor the
starters must be made attractive to existing players by inclusion of
new cards. Which leads me to my compromise position of *more*
starter only cards in the starters so that I feel I'm getting more
than 2 new vamps that I can't get in boosters and a few good reprints
I might want. (to my minds 2 or 3 per deck).

Its too bad statistics like what % of starters sold to new players are not
available to us, might make things clearer. I'ld guess around 20%.

-JTP

The lack of original product in the starters is an *excellent* thing.
That's how newer players get older cards. You wouldn't have to shell
out money for starters if you don't want -- if not for those $#@^!
two new vampires. *That's* the problem, not the reprinted cards in
the starters. I wish they'd stop doing that because it makes no
sense. It's hard for old players to ignore new vampires in starters that
we can't get in boosters. Yet it's also hard to buy the starters when
they're so full of stuff we don't need. As a result, we wind up feeling
robbed, somewhat. (I don't know. Does this irritate any other older
players as much as it does me?)

One thing they've done in the past the mitigates the problem a little
bit is to give out copies of those two controversial vampires (they've
been doing this since Sabbat War) as tournament party favors. Even so,
it would be much better if they just dropped the practice altogether.

Fred

> No "starter only" cards (which would mean to collect a set I would need
> only buy boosters)

In the past, the thinking on the newsgroup has been that starters were
the place to stick lots of good reprints for the newer players. That
concept works great because if you're trying to recruit new guys and
they see you playing lots of old, good cards, it helps to be able to
mention to them that they can get (at least some of) these cards by
buying this starter or that starter, just sitting right over there on
the retailer's shelf. Yet the older players don't have to get stuck
with reprints they have no need of by just not buying such starters.

Ergo, your second suggestion makes sense. The first one would tend to
gum up an otherwise good system.

Fred

Not sure whether that's true or not, exactly. But if WW is doing this to
force older players to buy starters, it sure is a nasty way to do so.

Fred

>Yet the older players don't have to get stuck

Q: If the only people buying starters are new players, and once you have
the starters, no new players will get them, how do you convince a store
to carry them in the first place?

A: By making them attractive for at least a copy or two for some of the
established players.

Providing some fixed new cards does that. They don't get "stuck" with
reprints - they can trade them away to the new players - but you get a
greater throughput of starters. If the oldbies don't want them in the
first place, the store won't order (many of? any of?) them and the new
players won't see them to buy them.

--
